approved: Adelaide Airport Curfew Amendment (Protecting Residents’ Amenity) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would stop the Transport Minister from allowing flights during the curfew's shoulder periods at Adelaide Airport.
It would repeal the part of the Adelaide Airport Curfew Act 2000 that lets the minister approve take-offs and landings between 11pm and midnight and from 5am to 6am.
The changes would apply to any take-off or landing after the bill starts, even if the minister had already approved it before then.
Removes the minister's power to permit international aircraft movements during the curfew shoulder periods.
Deletes the definition of international aircraft from the Act.
Removes the reporting requirement about international aircraft landing during the curfew.
Updates the delegation provision to remove reference to the repealed section 9.
Airlines and passengers using Adelaide Airport during the curfew shoulder periods.
